verizon_60_lines._note: Operator, 2026-09-09: the Verizon account is only 60 lines, not one per truck -- some owners supply their own tablet/line and should not be charged for one the company isn't providing. Operator also gave a reference price, same message: 'each tablet with line costs about $40'. No per-line Verizon bill exists in this corpus (the only per-line wireless CSV on file is STL TRUCKERS LLC's own account -- a different entity, see config/saas_app_charges.json -- not usable as a stand-in). Dividing each individual monthly AMEX invoice by $40 (not just the multi-month average) surfaces something real: the line count was NOT steady at 60 the whole time.

implied_line_count_by_invoice._note: AMEX 'VZWRLSS APOCC VISB' charges, individually, divided by $40 -- confirmed 2026-09-09.
implied_line_count_by_invoice.2025-10-31_through_2026-05-31: $2,360-2,371/month -> 59.0-59.1 lines, ROCK STEADY for 8 straight months -- matches the operator's stated 60 almost exactly
implied_line_count_by_invoice.conclusion: The account held at ~59 lines (matching the stated 60) from October 2025 through May 2026, then grew to ~70-72 lines by July 2026 -- an increase of 11-13 lines in roughly two months, worth ~$440-480/month more than the steady-state baseline. This is either legitimate fleet growth (new drivers/trucks added) or unaccounted growth worth investigating -- exactly the kind of creep the operator asked to catch. NOT YET EXPLAINED which.

verizon_60_lines.verizon_total_per_week_NOTE: This is the 47.7-week AVERAGE and blends the old ~59-line era with the new ~71-line one -- it understates the CURRENT run-rate. Use current_per_line below for where things stand now.

current_per_line._note: Based on the most recent invoice (2026-07-31, $2,868.73) and the operator's $40/line reference.

verizon_60_lines.sanity_check: Superseded by implied_line_count_by_invoice above -- the $46.13/month implied by the 47-week average was itself a symptom of blending two different eras together, not a stable per-line rate. The operator's own $40/line figure is the better anchor now that it can be checked against individual invoices instead of one long average.

coverage_gap._note: 90 trucks (17 AFG + 32 ZONE + 41 XTRACK, the same denominator used everywhere else in this file) minus the CURRENT ~72 lines leaves ~18 trucks presumptively on a driver-owned tablet, not 30 -- fewer than the historical estimate, because more company lines now exist. Consistent with the own_tablet_rate ($125) admin-fee variant already recorded below for drivers who supply their own hardware. WHICH specific trucks these are is not determinable from anything in this corpus; only a per-line Verizon export (device/user per line, like the PrePass CHARGESBYDEVICE CSV format) or each driver's actual admin-fee schedule from settlement data would identify them by name.

verizon_60_lines.how_to_apply: $10.61/truck/week applies ONLY to a truck whose driver has a company-provided tablet -- not uniformly across all 90 trucks the way the superseded $7.07 figure did. A driver on the own_tablet_rate ($125/month) schedule should carry $0 Verizon cost here, since they are already paying a different, higher flat fee that stands in for supplying their own device, not receiving both a discount rate AND a company tablet.

total_measured_per_truck_week._note: Sum of ifta + eld_software + transponders (per company) + samsara + verizon + pedigree_tpms (fleet-wide) -- Trippak excluded from every total since it is unmeasured, so every total below is a FLOOR, not the complete cost. STILL USES THE SUPERSEDED $7.07 flat Verizon spread, not verizon_60_lines' $10.61 -- which of each company's trucks actually hold one of the 60 lines is not known, so this fleet-average is kept as the conservative company-level figure rather than guessing a per-company split. Use verizon_60_lines directly for a specific truck known to have a company tablet.

admin_fee_actual_cost_per_truck_week.conclusion: Even missing Trippak entirely, real cost is now 1.9-2.6x the $23.09/week the admin fee actually charges (XTRACK 2.3x, ZONE 2.6x, AFG 1.9x) -- the fee does not cover what it was stated to cover, on the six of seven items that could be measured.
